reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it chiefly reviews the creator’s BitClub account after a period of mining and demonstrates how to buy a partial share from the account’s existing Bitcoin balance. The creator calls the arrangement passive income and includes a BitClub link, but the video does not make a concrete deceptive promise to viewers or expressly ask them to send money to the creator.

citations.quote: so how do we add partial shares to our bit code network so basically we have to login into our account
to just to demonstrate how do we do the repurchase

opening.argument: The video links an income outcome to acquiring a mining share. The speaker presents accumulated USD value after one month, describes the arrangement as passive income, and then announces a partial-share purchase. The on-screen workflow requires entering a BTC amount, selecting a mining pool, and pressing “Buy Partial Share,” while the page states that earnings will start after purchase. That is more than a neutral account review: it presents mining participation as the route to the claimed income and supplies a concrete purchase path.

citations.quote: So I have managed to accumulate this amount of value in USD in one month
this is indeed a passive income
today I'm going to do a small partial share purchase

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this a demonstration, but the demonstration itself is the solicitation mechanism. It shows a BTC-denominated amount, a selected mining pool, and a purchase button, while the narration connects partial shares to passive income and a 600-day earning period. A viewer does not need to be told to send money to the creator personally for the video to direct them toward buying the promoted mining product.

citations.quote: every partial shares will last for 600 days and this is indeed a passive income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The purchase screen shows an account-holder workflow, not proof that viewers were promised a return or asked to transfer funds to the speaker. The narration describes what the creator did in an existing account, and the visible result is merely an invoice notice. The quoted “passive income” language is a characterization, but it does not establish that the mining service was deceptive or that the displayed earnings would be delivered to viewers.

citations.quote: I've been doing this thing for the past one month
this is indeed a passive income

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency payment, a minimum BTC purchase, a long 600-day contract, recurring mining-earnings entries, and a passive-income framing. The speaker says the minimum is 0.01 BTC and the interface accepts that amount for a mining pool share. The account page also displays repeated mining-earnings records. Taken together, these features frame a paid mining package as an ongoing income source while requiring users to commit crypto for an extended period.

citations.quote: but I have a continuous contract of 600 days
this is indeed a passive income
minimum cheese is 0.01 btc

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes that there is no explicit personal request for money, but that omits the stronger risk pattern visible in the product flow. The viewer is shown a minimum BTC commitment for a mining-pool share, promised ongoing earnings, and a 600-day duration. A crypto payment requirement and recurring return display are precisely the features that make this promotional income claim materially risky, even without a direct wallet address in the narration.

citations.quote: every partial shares will last for 600 days and this is indeed a passive income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals establish only that the video discusses a crypto mining product and shows its account interface. The repeated entries are displayed account records, not independent proof that returns were guaranteed, fixed, or deceptive. The 600-day term and the passive-income description likewise do not show that the service failed to perform. Risk indicators alone cannot convert an operational demonstration into evidence of a scam.

citations.quote: this is indeed a passive income
every partial shares will last for 600 days

opening.argument: Although presented as a review and tutorial, the video functions as promotion. Its title advertises a “25 days mining review,” the description directs viewers to a BitClub link, and the narration reports the creator’s accumulated USD value before walking through a new partial-share purchase. The screen then shows the exact amount, pool selection, and purchase control needed to participate. This combination gives viewers both a favorable testimonial and an operational route into the paid mining program.

citations.quote: bitclub network 25 days mining review
check out http://bitclub.network/knightbit ...
So I have managed to accumulate this amount of value in USD in one month

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material an account review does not neutralize its promotional effect. The description supplies an external BitClub link, the narration highlights accumulated value and passive income, and the tutorial ends at a purchase interface with a BTC amount and buy control. Those elements steer viewers toward participation even if the speaker never uses the words “send me money.”

citations.quote: check out http://bitclub.network/knightbit ...
this is indeed a passive income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title and link identify the subject and where the account can be accessed, but they do not establish a deceptive promise. The video can reasonably be understood as documenting the creator’s own account and explaining its controls. The purchase page demonstrates functionality, while the quoted earnings language describes the creator’s experience rather than proving viewers would receive the same result.
